questions.q: What is the purpose of writing `device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")` once at the top of a script?
options: It permanently disables the CPU
It makes the script device-agnostic, running correctly whether or not a GPU is present, by reusing one variable everywhere
It is required syntax with no functional effect
It converts all tensors to float16 automatically
questions.explain: Checking availability once and reusing the resulting device variable throughout the script means the same code runs unchanged on a GPU-equipped machine or a CPU-only one.

questions.q: What does calling model.to(device) do, versus tensor.to(device)?
options: Both behave identically and return a brand-new copy
model.to(device) moves the model's parameters and buffers in place and returns the same object; tensor.to(device) returns a (generally) new tensor on that device
model.to(device) only works on CPU; tensor.to(device) only works on GPU
model.to(device) deletes the original model
questions.explain: For an nn.Module, .to(device) mutates the module in place (moving all parameters/buffers) and returns the same object. For a plain tensor, .to(device) returns a tensor on the new device rather than mutating in place.

questions.q: You get 'RuntimeError: Expected all tensors to be on the same device...'. What is the most common cause?
options: A syntax error in the model definition
The model was moved to the GPU but an input batch, label tensor, or newly created tensor was left on the CPU (often from forgetting a device= argument)
The GPU driver is corrupted
The batch size is too large
questions.explain: PyTorch never silently moves data between devices. This error almost always traces back to one tensor (input, label, or a freshly created one without device=) still sitting on a different device than the rest of the computation.

questions.q: What is the advantage of torch.zeros(4, 4, device=device) over torch.zeros(4, 4).to(device)?
options: There is no difference in behavior or performance
It avoids creating the tensor on the CPU first and then copying it, by creating it directly on the target device
It produces a tensor with different values
It only works for integer tensors
questions.explain: Passing device= to a creation function allocates the tensor directly on the target device, skipping the extra CPU-to-GPU copy that .to(device) would otherwise require.

questions.q: What is the `mps` backend in PyTorch?
options: A CPU-only fallback mode
A debugging tool for autograd
The backend for running PyTorch on Apple Silicon GPUs via Metal Performance Shaders
A distributed training protocol
questions.explain: mps is PyTorch's device backend for Apple Silicon GPUs. It's checked with torch.backends.mps.is_available() and used with the same .to(device) pattern as cuda.
